column1: # Owner: board #3677. Consumers: #3687 (river traits) / #2968 (province terrains) / mapgen/tabulate_state_prior.py (canon_river) / mapgen/validate_map.py (reads river and state_key by header name).
# One row per (river + state). The traced map_data/rivers.png is unnamed and incomplete so this hand-authored layer is the canon river source.
# validate_map.py warns (never errors) where a river is not in rivers_index.json: pin the name through canon_river_names.json (handoff to #3703/#3687).

# Source grammar as in state_climate_classes.csv: lex:<Page>#<section> (zone | zone via hub X | zone via owner TAG | realm) [GW publication the page footnotes]; name (...) = the state's canon name carries the river.

# Tier A = an extract places the river in the state by name or hub or the state is named for the river feature itself. Tier B = the state is named for the river's province and the extract only describes the river.
# Tier C = [unverified]: nothing in the extracts; no climate class or override may rest on a C row. Lexicanum pages were read 2026-10-04 and are paraphrased - never quoted.
# These comment lines carry no comma on purpose: validate_map.py's reader does not skip comment lines and would read a comma-bearing one as a row.
# After editing re-run: python mapgen/tabulate_state_prior.py --classes mapgen/config/state_climate_classes.csv --rivers mapgen/config/canon_rivers.csv --markdown
